judged_text: In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response that is assigned to the HubspotToken-typed variable, so .access_token, .refresh_token and .expires_in are all undefined when the new credential is computed and persisted. Hubspot stores a credential with undefined tokens and a NaN expiry_date, silently breaking the integration in sharing deployments with no error at refresh time — failures surface later as confusing 401s.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sharing mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), the function does `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then (immediately after the shown diff context) computes expiry and updates credentials based on token fields. With a raw `Response`, `hubspotRefreshToken.access_token` / `refresh_token` / `expires_in` will be `undefined` at runtime unless the code explicitly parses JSON first (it doesn’t here), leading to persisting invalid/NaN-derived credential data in sharing deployments. This mismatch is directly verifiable from the diff.
